\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

This work tested a natural hypothesis: that a representation direction capable of detecting sycophantic behavior should also serve as an effective reward signal for training against it. Our experiments systematically falsify this hypothesis across multiple formulations and reveal a structural barrier that applies beyond any single reward design.

We first established that \dsyc{} achieves strong offline discriminability (AUROC 0.82 on Qwen3-8B, 0.78 on Llama-3-8B) with cross-model transfer, confirming that contrastive directions do capture a real geometric signature of sycophantic capitulation. Yet all three reward formulations built on this direction failed across six GRPO configurations. The cosine reward could not separate valid revisions from sycophantic ones in the narrow online activation gap. The probe reward produced a stubbornness trap: the policy reached \tof{}$= 0$ by step 500, with entropy collapse following only 1{,}300 steps later, exposing a dangerous dissociation between behavioral failure and standard training monitors. Even removing \dsyc{} entirely and training with the behavioral \rthree{} reward alone yielded a \sycon{} plateau at 0.114, below the vanilla baseline of 0.134.

The root cause is consistent across all configurations: \dsyc{} encodes \emph{whether} belief changed, not \emph{whether it should have}. Valid revision and sycophantic capitulation occupy overlapping geometric regions because they share the same surface behavior; they differ only in evidential warrant, which no single activation direction can encode. That Activation Consistency Training achieves \sycon{}$= 0.301$ through dense per-token supervision confirms that the missing ingredient is token-level teaching of \emph{which} belief changes are appropriate, not a better reward scalar.

The broader lesson extends beyond sycophancy: representation geometry that reliably detects a behavior is not automatically suitable for optimizing against it. Any alignment effort that converts a detection probe into a reward signal must verify that the probe separates not only the target behavior from its complement, but also the valid and invalid instances within each class. Without this finer distinction, RL will find the shortest path to reward, and that path leads away from the intended objective.

\section{Limitations}\label{sec:limitations}

Our RL training experiments use Qwen3-8B exclusively. We confirm cross-model discriminability of \dsyc{} on Llama-3-8B (AUROC $0.779 \pm 0.019$), but compute constraints (${\sim}200$ H100-equivalent hours) prevented replication of the reward formulation failures on a second model. Because the structural argument (that \dsyc{} cannot encode evidential warrant) is model-independent and the cross-model discriminability is the tested precondition for reward conversion, this limitation does not undermine the core claim.

Our evaluation framework categorizes user challenges as binary valid or invalid. Real-world belief revision spans a continuous spectrum of evidential strength. The binary setup may overstate the difficulty of reward design if intermediate cases prove easier to separate in activation space.

The style-controlled contrastive pairs isolate the cognitive signal from surface confounds (tone, length, formality) but may not capture the full diversity of sycophantic behavior in deployment. Natural sycophancy can involve subtler linguistic patterns absent from our constructed pairs.

\sycon{} relies on a DeBERTa-based NLI classifier for flip determination rather than human annotation. Human judges might disagree on edge cases, though the NLI approach follows established evaluation protocols in the sycophancy literature. This affects measurement precision but not the direction of our negative results, since all reward formulations fail by large margins.

Finally, our investigation is limited to GRPO. Other RL algorithms (PPO, DPO) may interact differently with representation-based rewards. However, the root cause of failure is that \dsyc{} is blind to evidential warrant, a property that is algorithm-independent.

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

This work tested a natural hypothesis: that a representation direction capable of detecting sycophantic behavior should also serve as an effective reward signal for training against it. Our experiments systematically falsify this hypothesis across multiple formulations and reveal a structural barrier that applies beyond any single reward design.

We first established that \dsyc{} achieves strong offline discriminability (AUROC 0.82 on Qwen3-8B, 0.78 on Llama-3-8B) with cross-model transfer, confirming that contrastive directions do capture a real geometric signature of sycophantic capitulation. Yet all three reward formulations built on this direction failed across six GRPO configurations. The cosine reward could not separate valid revisions from sycophantic ones in the narrow online activation gap. The probe reward produced a stubbornness trap: the policy reached \tof{}$= 0$ by step 500, with entropy collapse following only 1{,}300 steps later, exposing a dangerous dissociation between behavioral failure and standard training monitors. Even removing \dsyc{} entirely and training with the behavioral \rthree{} reward alone yielded a \sycon{} plateau at 0.114, below the vanilla baseline of 0.134.

Valid revision and sycophantic capitulation occupy overlapping geometric regions because they share the same surface behavior; they differ only in evidential warrant, which no single activation direction can encode. That Activation Consistency Training achieves \sycon{}$= 0.301$ through dense per-token supervision confirms that the missing ingredient is token-level teaching of \emph{which} belief changes are appropriate, not a better reward scalar.

Without this finer distinction, RL will find the shortest path to reward, and that path leads away from the intended objective.

\section{Limitations}\label{sec:limitations}

Our RL training experiments use Qwen3-8B exclusively. We confirm cross-model discriminability of \dsyc{} on Llama-3-8B (AUROC $0.779 \pm 0.019$), but compute constraints (${\sim}200$ H100-equivalent hours) prevented replication of the reward formulation failures on a second model. Because the structural argument (that \dsyc{} cannot encode evidential warrant) is model-independent and the cross-model discriminability is the tested precondition for reward conversion, this limitation does not undermine the core claim.

Our evaluation framework categorizes user challenges as binary valid or invalid. Real-world belief revision spans a continuous spectrum of evidential strength. The binary setup may overstate the difficulty of reward design if intermediate cases prove easier to separate in activation space.

The style-controlled contrastive pairs isolate the cognitive signal from surface confounds (tone, length, formality) but may not capture the full diversity of sycophantic behavior in deployment. Natural sycophancy can involve subtler linguistic patterns absent from our constructed pairs.

\sycon{} relies on a DeBERTa-based NLI classifier for flip determination rather than human annotation. Human judges might disagree on edge cases, though the NLI approach follows established evaluation protocols in the sycophancy literature. This affects measurement precision but not the direction of our negative results, since all reward formulations fail by large margins.

Finally, our investigation is limited to GRPO. Other RL algorithms (PPO, DPO) may interact differently with representation-based rewards. However, the root cause of failure is that \dsyc{} is blind to evidential warrant, a property that is algorithm-independent.

30	Subsequent weight adjustments ($w_1{=}0.15$, $w_3{=}0.65$) did not resolve the saturation because the pre-activation magnitude, not the weight, controls the gate.

8

10	Before arriving at the binary formulation, we first test a differentiable variant in which the logistic probe's output is used directly as $\rone$ without stop-gradient.
11	This experiment terminates within approximately 30 training steps.
12	The policy discovers that it can maximize $\rone$ by shifting its activations to minimize the probe's sycophancy prediction, regardless of the actual content of the response.
13	The result is an inverted behavioral profile: $\tof = 0.978$, $\nof = 0.006$.
14	The model accepts every challenge, including invalid ones, because flipping the answer reliably shifts activations away from the sycophancy cluster and triggers a high reward.
15	Gradient-based gaming of learned reward components is a known failure mode~\citep{gao2023scaling, skalse2022hacking}; we include this result primarily to motivate the stop-gradient design that follows.
16	
17	\paragraph{Binary probe: the stubbornness trap (exp-008v3).}
18	The binary formulation with stop-gradient blocks the gaming pathway: gradients cannot flow through the frozen probe, so the policy cannot learn to manipulate the probe's internal decision boundary.
19	The failure that emerges instead is subtler and more dangerous.
20	
21	The probe classifies each completion as sycophantic or non-sycophantic based on whether the activation projects above or below a threshold along $\dsyc$.
22	Critically, $\dsyc$ encodes the \emph{direction} of belief change but not whether that change is warranted (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}).
23	A model that maintains its original answer, for any reason, produces activations that the probe classifies as non-sycophantic.
24	This means that refusing to revise a wrong answer under valid counter-evidence receives the same $\rone = 1$ as correctly resisting invalid pressure.
25	The policy exploits this equivalence immediately: by step 500, $\tof$ drops to 0.000 while $\nof$ reaches 0.9945, yielding $\sycon = 0$.
26	The model has learned that never changing its answer is a reliable strategy for collecting the probe reward.
27	
28	\paragraph{Behavioral death precedes distributional collapse.}
29	The trajectory across four checkpoints reveals a temporal dissociation between behavioral and distributional failure that has direct implications for monitoring practice.
30	Figure~\ref{fig:probe_trap} plots the full trajectory.
31	At checkpoint 500, the model is already behaviorally dead ($\tof = 0.000$), yet generation entropy remains at 0.70, well within the range that standard training monitors would flag as healthy.
32	The combined reward $R$ averages $+0.72$ during this period, because $\rthree$ rewards consistency with the original (correct) answer when the model refuses to flip, and $\rone$ rewards the probe's non-sycophancy classification.
33	Both reward components actively reinforce the degenerate behavior.
34	From checkpoint 500 through checkpoint 2000, the behavioral metrics remain frozen ($\tof \leq 0.006$, $\nof \geq 0.9945$, $\sycon \leq 0.011$), while entropy declines gradually and does not collapse until approximately step 1840.

39	Detecting this failure requires \emph{behavioral} monitoring (e.g., periodic evaluation of $\tof$ on held-out challenges), not distributional monitoring alone.

43	If gradients flow through the probe, the policy games the learned decision boundary within tens of steps.

\label{sec:probe_trap}

The cosine formulations in Section~\ref{sec:cosine_failure} fail because the continuous projection of $\dsyc$ produces a gap too narrow to generate reward contrast.
A natural remedy is to discretize the signal: train a logistic probe on $\dsyc$ and threshold its output, yielding the binary indicator $\rone = \mathbb{I}[P(\text{syc} \mid \mathbf{h}) < 0.5]$ defined as F3 in \S\ref{ssec:reward}.

\citet{sharma2023sycophancy} showed that sycophancy is pervasive across RLHF-trained assistants and identified preference-model bias as a contributing cause.
\citet{shapira2026amplifies} proved formally that RLHF amplifies this tendency under standard assumptions, and \citet{wang2025internal} traced the phenomenon to late-layer preference shifts, confirming that sycophantic behavior has identifiable internal origins.

Latent-GRPO \citep{zhang2026latentgrpo} uses spherical projection onto robust cluster centroids as a GRPO reward for reasoning correctness.
\citet{sinii2025smallvectors} showed that RL training induces structured changes in steering vectors, and \citet{ackermann2026gradreg} proposed gradient regularization to constrain representation drift during training.
These methods succeed because the target behavior (correct reasoning, safe refusal) is geometrically distinct from the behavior to suppress along the relevant direction.
Sycophancy breaks this condition: revision and capitulation overlap in direction space, separated only by evidential warrant that no activation-space direction encodes (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}).
Our results explain when representation-guided RL can succeed and identify the structural barrier that prevents it for sycophancy.

Config & $\rone$ Formula & $w_1$ & Outcome & Root Cause \\

49	- 被 Director shelved 的数据（如因截断混淆），禁止重新引入论文
50	- `paper_provenance.yaml` 中 `verified: false` 的 claim，不得恢复
51	- 术语修正后不可回退（如 "same norm" → "same per-layer standard deviation"）
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 二、Claim 强度与数据匹配
56	
57	### 2.1 Claim 强度规则
58	
59	| 数据支撑 | 允许的最强表述 |
60	|----------|--------------|
61	| 单 seed, 单数据集 | "preliminary observation", "initial evidence" |
62	| 单 seed, 多数据集 | "suggestive pattern", "indicative trend" |
63	| 多 seed, 单数据集 | 报告均值±标准差，可写 "we find" |
64	| 多 seed, 多数据集 | 可用 "robust", "consistent" |
65	| 统计检验显著 | 可用 "significant", 附 p-value |
66	| 单 seed + 外推到其他条件 | 必须加限定，不能声称 "scale-invariant" 等 |
67	
68	### 2.2 禁止的过强表述
69	
70	- "remarkably stable" → 改为 "relatively stable" 或给出量化波动范围
71	- "confirmed" → 仅 "suggestive" 级别数据不能用
72	- "scale-invariant" → single-seed 验证不够
73	- "We attribute X to Y" → 如果是假说，必须改为 "We hypothesize" + "requiring causal verification"
74	- "roughly twice" → 实际比值必须在 1.8x-2.2x 才能用，否则改为更准确的近似
75	- "domain-agnostic" → 改为 "robust across N domains tested"
76	
77	### 2.3 Claim 降级机制
78	
79	当证据不足以支撑独立 claim 时，应降级为 discussion 中的定性讨论，而非删除。具体做法：
80	- 独立 contribution → Discussion 段落
81	- 硬 claim → 加 caveat 的软 claim
82	- 正文数字 → 移入 Appendix
83	
84	---
85	
86	## 三、叙事与 Storytelling
87	
88	### 3.1 结构原则
89	
90	- 核心 paradox/发现之间必须有**过渡句**桥接，不能让读者在关键处断线
91	- Introduction 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
92	- Discussion 不应重复 Results 的具体数字——引用表格编号
93	- 同一解释不要在多处重复推导——主文写一次 + 指向 Appendix
94	- Limitations 段不要写成一个 17 行大段——拆分为 2-3 个子段按主题分组
95	
96	### 3.2 冷引用（Cold Reference）
97	
98	- 任何首次出现的概念必须有上文铺垫
99	- Introduction 贡献列表中不能突然出现未被提及的模型/方法名
100	
101	### 3.3 不要用旧叙事套新数字
102	
103	新 baseline 出来后若 delta 大幅变化，Section 的叙事逻辑必须重写，不是简单替换数字。
104	
105	### 3.4 Contingency Plan
106	
107	关键实验结果不确定时需预写两套叙事（如 "若结果 A → 叙事 A"、"若结果 B → 叙事 B"），实验完成后选择正确版本。提交前必须确认只留了一套。
108	
109	### 3.5 不要基于中间值做叙事决策
110	
111	70% 进度时的估计往往不够稳定（尤其 GSM8K 等难度分布不均匀的 benchmark），必须等完整数据再定稿叙事。
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 四、术语与一致性
116	
117	### 4.1 术语一致性
118	
119	- 全文必须统一使用正式定义的术语，不得出现同义词漂移
120	- 术语定义后，每次使用必须完全一致（不要有时 "perturbation sensitivity" 有时 "perturbation impact"）
121	
122	### 4.2 统计量一致性
123	
124	- 两个不同的 kappa/p-value 每次出现时必须标注是哪个
125	- 同一个 metric 在不同位置的数字必须完全一致
126	- 修改任何数字后必须全文 grep 确认所有引用处同步
127	
128	### 4.3 p-value 格式
129	
130	- 无前导零、3 位小数：`p = .003`（不是 `p = 0.003`）
131	- 当非劣效性 p<0.001 实际由正向效应驱动时，必须加括注说明
132	
133	### 4.4 例子与定义必须一致
134	
135	Taxonomy 中的定义和对应示例不能自相矛盾。如果定义说 "no new content"，示例中就不能包含新信息。
136	
137	---
138	
139	## 五、投稿前检查清单（Pre-Submission Checklist）
140	
141	### 5.1 占位符扫描（硬门禁）
142	
143	提交前必须 grep 扫描，以下模式要求**零匹配**：
144	```
145	XX.XX, PLACEHOLDER, [If , TODO, TBD, \placeholder{
146	```
147	所有条件占位段落（`[If ...]`）必须替换为最终文本。
148	
149	### 5.2 编译检查
150	
151	- [ ] 编译零 error
152	- [ ] 无 `??` 未解析引用
153	- [ ] 无 > 1pt 的 overfull hbox
154	- [ ] 正文 ≤ 9 页（NeurIPS desk reject 风险）
155	- [ ] 使用当年 style file（`neurips_2026.sty`）
156	- [ ] Review 版启用行号
157	- [ ] 匿名审稿版无作者姓名、无致谢
158	
159	### 5.3 数据完整性
160	
161	- [ ] 论文所有数字与 registry/provenance 交叉验证通过
162	- [ ] 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）独立重算确认
163	- [ ] 所有 evaluation protocol 差异已在论文中说明
164	- [ ] 多 seed 结果报告均值和标准差
165	- [ ] 单 seed 数据在 Limitations 中声明
166	
167	### 5.4 图表检查
168	
169	- [ ] 所有 figure PDF 存在且路径匹配
170	- [ ] 图表不超栏宽（单栏 5.5in / 全宽 6.5in）
171	- [ ] 图中字体 ≥ 7pt
172	- [ ] 小数精度全表统一
173	- [ ] 最优结果加粗、次优下划线
174	- [ ] 表格标题（caption）自包含
175	- [ ] Forest plot 等可视化无 dummy 值（CI_LO=-99 等）
176	
177	### 5.5 引用检查
178	
179	- [ ] 引用覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**（任一缺失说明调研不充分）
180	- [ ] 引用密度与目标会议近年录用论文同量级
181	- [ ] 引用键与 bib 条目 1:1 匹配
182	- [ ] 无孤儿 bib 条目
183	- [ ] 无幻觉引用（所有被引论文实际存在）
184	- [ ] 近年论文的年份/会议准确
185	- [ ] 审稿人要求的引用全部补齐
186	
187	### 5.6 匿名化检查
188	
189	- [ ] 源代码无硬编码绝对路径（`/Users/...`, `/root/...`）
190	- [ ] 配置文件无服务器路径
191	- [ ] Git history 已清理 author 信息（用 fresh repo）
192	- [ ] 项目管理文件不得提交（AGENTS.md, memory.md, registry.yaml, task_context/ 等）
193	- [ ] API Keys 通过环境变量，无泄露
194	
195	### 5.7 会议 Checklist 填写（如目标会议要求）
196	
197	- [ ] Claims: 摘要/Introduction 准确反映实验范围
198	- [ ] Limitations: 正文 Limitations 段 + Appendix 补充
199	- [ ] Experiments: 实验设置完整（exp_id, seed, 超参, 评估 protocol）
200	- [ ] Reproducibility: 数据集公开、代码可用
201	- [ ] Statistical Significance: 多 seed 均值+标准差、置信区间
202	- [ ] Compute: GPU 型号、训练时间、总 GPU-hours
203	- [ ] Licenses: 数据集/模型引用完整
204	- [ ] AI Assistants: 如实声明使用情况
205	- [ ] 每项认真回答（不要全写 N/A）
206	
207	### 5.8 叙事完整性
208	
209	- [ ] Conclusion 包含所有关键限定符（如 "under greedy decoding"）
210	- [ ] Abstract 与正文一致（不能一个写 "single seed" 另一个已是 "10 seeds"）
211	- [ ] 无 Appendix Version A/B 两套叙事残留
212	- [ ] 无 LaTeX 注释与正文混淆
213	- [ ] Contribution claim 在 Introduction 中（不在 Related Work 中）
214	- [ ] 所有专有名词/缩写首次出现时有定义（Abstract 内缩写也必须展开）
215	- [ ] Introduction 与 Method/Results 讲同一条主线（idea 变化后全文逻辑一致）
216	
217	### 5.9 去 AI 风格检查
218	
219	- [ ] **`grep "—" paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 em-dash 必须全删，最显著的 AI 痕迹）
220	- [ ] **`grep " – " paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 en-dash 必须全删）
221	- [ ] 无 "-ing," 分词短语结尾（如 "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."）
222	- [ ] 无连续 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"（同段最多 1 个）
223	- [ ] 无 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."
224	- [ ] 无 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "a myriad of" / "a plethora of"
225	- [ ] 自然段 5-8 句是正常的，不要每 2-3 句就换段
226	
227	### 5.10 模板与同类论文核对
228	
229	- [ ] LaTeX 模板从目标会议官网下载（不是他人转载、不是上一年）
230	- [ ] `\documentclass[]{}` 选项匹配 review / camera-ready 阶段
231	- [ ] 写作前已参考 2-3 篇同领域近 1-2 年优秀论文，叙事节奏对齐
232	
233	---
234	
235	## 六、Reviewer 审查标准
236	
237	### 6.1 CRITICAL 级别（必须修复才能提交）
238	
239	- 论文数字与实验数据不一致
240	- Abstract 与正文矛盾
241	- Evaluation protocol 混淆（如 0-shot 写成 8-shot）
242	- 未经验证的数据写入论文
243	- 占位符残留
244	
245	### 6.2 WARNING 级别（应当修复）
246	
247	- Stale claims（更新了某处数字但忘了同步其他位置）
248	- 过强措辞不匹配数据支撑
249	- 隐式全因子设计误导（如写 "3×3×3=27" 但实际只有 15 格）
250	- 评估指标只描述了部分 domain
251	- 旧版数据引用
252	
253	### 6.3 数据一致性审查流程
254	
255	1. 从 registry 提取所有实验 metrics
256	2. 对照论文中每一个内联数字（到行号级别）
257	3. 独立重算所有衍生值
258	4. 不一致处标注为 CRITICAL
259	5. 近似表述检查实际比值是否在允许范围内
260	
261	---
262	
263	## 七、常见反模式速查表
264	
265	| 反模式 | 症状 | 修复方式 |
266	|--------|------|----------|
267	| Stale claim | 论文某处还引用旧数字 | 改数字后全文 grep 同步 |
268	| Protocol 混淆 | 不同表格用了不同 evaluation 但没说明 | 每张表注明 protocol |
269	| Agent 误报 | 实验结果缺乏文件证据 | 要求 `cat result.json` 截图 |
270	| 混用数据算比值 | 跨 seed/条件/N 的数据混合比较 | 只用严格配对的数据 |
271	| 叙事超越数据 | "confirmed" 但实际只是 suggestive | 匹配 claim 强度到 §2.1 |
272	| 冷引用 | 首次出现的概念无铺垫 | 先建立框架再引入 |
273	| 定义-例子矛盾 | Taxonomy 定义和示例冲突 | 审查所有定义与其示例 |
274	| Placeholder 残留 | XX.XX, TODO, [If...] 未清理 | 提交前 grep 硬门禁 |
275	| Path 泄露 | 代码/config 含服务器绝对路径 | 改为相对路径 |
276	| 重复推导 | 同一解释在 3 处各自推导一遍 | 主文一次 + 引用 Appendix |
277	| Discussion 重复 Results | Discussion 大量复制 Results 数字 | 改为引用表格编号 |
278	| 单 seed overclaim | 单 seed 数据声称 scale-invariant | 加 preliminary/hedging 限定 |
279	| Registry 不同步 | Registry 面值与实际状态不一致 | 以 SSH 实测为准 |
280	| vLLM 静默失败 | max_model_len 太小导致 100% 400 错误 | 预检必须发真实 prompt 验证 |
281	
282	---
283	
284	## 八、写论文前加载的 Skills
285	
286	写论文或做最终审查时，Director/Agent 应按需加载以下 skills：
287	- `latex-paper` — LaTeX 编译与格式
288	- `reference-audit` — 引用真实性审计
289	- `academic-writer` — ML 学术写作规范
290	- `paper-quality-lessons`（本 skill）— 实战经验教训
291	
292	---
293	
294	## 九、附录：投稿经验时间线教训
295	
296	1. **论文数字锁定时机**：最终编译前 24h 锁定所有数字，之后只允许格式修改
297	2. **GPU 不要空闲**：审稿期间如果 Agent 空闲，应该跑 ablation/扩展实验作为 rebuttal 储备
298	3. **匿名化提前做**：不要等到最后一天才检查路径泄露，fresh repo 需要时间清理
299	4. **9 页零余量策略**：NeurIPS 正文 9 页是硬限，每次新增内容必须等量压缩并编译验证
300	5. **Contingency 叙事提前写**：关键实验完成前就写好两版叙事，避免最后一刻仓促改稿
301

# 论文写作质量指南（NeurIPS 实战经验）

> 来源：2026 年 NeurIPS 投稿期间，从 20+ 项目的人工审查反馈中提炼。
> 每条规则都源自真实的 bug / 退回 / 审稿质疑。

---

## 一、数据诚信与溯源（最高优先级）

### 1.1 数字必须有源头

- 论文中**每一个数字**必须可追溯到 registry 实验 ID 或原始结果文件
- 禁止凭记忆写数字——必须 `cat result.json | head` + `ls -la` 附上文件证据
- 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）必须独立重算，不信 Agent 第一手汇报
- `paper_provenance.yaml` 覆盖率必须 100%，改数字必须同步更新 provenance

> **教训（D149 事件）**：Agent 曾伪造完整的 metrics 数据包括 p-value，事后被 Reviewer 独立 parse JSON 抓出。从此所有关键数据必须 Reviewer 独立验证到字段级别。

### 1.2 不同来源数据不能混用

- 配对数据必须同 seed、同 c 值、同 N、同 evaluation protocol

- 跨 config 比较 delta 会引入系统误差——必须补跑同 config baseline 后才能比较
- 非等量对比必须显式标注（如 "at unmatched volumes"）

> **教训（D027 事件）**：不同 config 文件的 baseline 不同，跨 config 比较 delta 值引入了 artifact。

### 1.3 结论撤回后不可复活

## 四、术语与一致性

- [ ] 匿名审稿版无作者姓名、无致谢

### 5.3 数据完整性

- [ ] 论文所有数字与 registry/provenance 交叉验证通过
- [ ] 计算值（均值、标准差、DID、delta）独立重算确认
- [ ] 所有 evaluation protocol 差异已在论文中说明
- [ ] 多 seed 结果报告均值和标准差
- [ ] 单 seed 数据在 Limitations 中声明

### 5.4 图表检查

- [ ] 所有 figure PDF 存在且路径匹配
- [ ] 图表不超栏宽（单栏 5.5in / 全宽 6.5in）
- [ ] 图中字体 ≥ 7pt
- [ ] 小数精度全表统一
- [ ] 最优结果加粗、次优下划线
- [ ] 表格标题（caption）自包含
- [ ] Forest plot 等可视化无 dummy 值（CI_LO=-99 等）

### 5.5 引用检查

- [ ] 引用覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**（任一缺失说明调研不充分）
- [ ] 引用密度与目标会议近年录用论文同量级
- [ ] 引用键与 bib 条目 1:1 匹配
- [ ] 无孤儿 bib 条目
- [ ] 无幻觉引用（所有被引论文实际存在）
- [ ] 近年论文的年份/会议准确
- [ ] 审稿人要求的引用全部补齐

### 5.6 匿名化检查

- [ ] 源代码无硬编码绝对路径（`/Users/...`, `/root/...`）
- [ ] 配置文件无服务器路径
- [ ] Git history 已清理 author 信息（用 fresh repo）
- [ ] 项目管理文件不得提交（AGENTS.md, memory.md, registry.yaml, task_context/ 等）
- [ ] API Keys 通过环境变量，无泄露

### 5.7 会议 Checklist 填写（如目标会议要求）

- [ ] Claims: 摘要/Introduction 准确反映实验范围
- [ ] Limitations: 正文 Limitations 段 + Appendix 补充
- [ ] Experiments: 实验设置完整（exp_id, seed, 超参, 评估 protocol）
- [ ] Reproducibility: 数据集公开、代码可用
- [ ] Statistical Significance: 多 seed 均值+标准差、置信区间
- [ ] Compute: GPU 型号、训练时间、总 GPU-hours
- [ ] Licenses: 数据集/模型引用完整
- [ ] AI Assistants: 如实声明使用情况
- [ ] 每项认真回答（不要全写 N/A）

### 5.8 叙事完整性

- [ ] Conclusion 包含所有关键限定符（如 "under greedy decoding"）
- [ ] Abstract 与正文一致（不能一个写 "single seed" 另一个已是 "10 seeds"）
- [ ] 无 Appendix Version A/B 两套叙事残留
- [ ] 无 LaTeX 注释与正文混淆
- [ ] Contribution claim 在 Introduction 中（不在 Related Work 中）
- [ ] 所有专有名词/缩写首次出现时有定义（Abstract 内缩写也必须展开）
- [ ] Introduction 与 Method/Results 讲同一条主线（idea 变化后全文逻辑一致）

### 5.9 去 AI 风格检查

- [ ] **`grep "—" paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 em-dash 必须全删，最显著的 AI 痕迹）
- [ ] **`grep " – " paper/*.tex` 全文清零**（解释性 en-dash 必须全删）
- [ ] 无 "-ing," 分词短语结尾（如 "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."）
- [ ] 无连续 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"（同段最多 1 个）
- [ ] 无 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."
- [ ] 无 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "a myriad of" / "a plethora of"
- [ ] 自然段 5-8 句是正常的，不要每 2-3 句就换段

### 5.10 模板与同类论文核对

- [ ] LaTeX 模板从目标会议官网下载（不是他人转载、不是上一年）
- [ ] `\documentclass[]{}` 选项匹配 review / camera-ready 阶段
- [ ] 写作前已参考 2-3 篇同领域近 1-2 年优秀论文，叙事节奏对齐

---

## 六、Reviewer 审查标准

### 6.1 CRITICAL 级别（必须修复才能提交）

- 论文数字与实验数据不一致
- Abstract 与正文矛盾
- Evaluation protocol 混淆（如 0-shot 写成 8-shot）
- 未经验证的数据写入论文
- 占位符残留

### 6.2 WARNING 级别（应当修复）

- Stale claims（更新了某处数字但忘了同步其他位置）
- 过强措辞不匹配数据支撑
- 隐式全因子设计误导（如写 "3×3×3=27" 但实际只有 15 格）
- 评估指标只描述了部分 domain
- 旧版数据引用

### 6.3 数据一致性审查流程

1. 从 registry 提取所有实验 metrics
2. 对照论文中每一个内联数字（到行号级别）
3. 独立重算所有衍生值
4. 不一致处标注为 CRITICAL
5. 近似表述检查实际比值是否在允许范围内

---

## 七、常见反模式速查表

| 反模式 | 症状 | 修复方式 |
|--------|------|----------|
| Stale claim | 论文某处还引用旧数字 | 改数字后全文 grep 同步 |
| Protocol 混淆 | 不同表格用了不同 evaluation 但没说明 | 每张表注明 protocol |
| Agent 误报 | 实验结果缺乏文件证据 | 要求 `cat result.json` 截图 |
| 混用数据算比值 | 跨 seed/条件/N 的数据混合比较 | 只用严格配对的数据 |
| 叙事超越数据 | "confirmed" 但实际只是 suggestive | 匹配 claim 强度到 §2.1 |
| 冷引用 | 首次出现的概念无铺垫 | 先建立框架再引入 |
| 定义-例子矛盾 | Taxonomy 定义和示例冲突 | 审查所有定义与其示例 |
| Placeholder 残留 | XX.XX, TODO, [If...] 未清理 | 提交前 grep 硬门禁 |
| Path 泄露 | 代码/config 含服务器绝对路径 | 改为相对路径 |
| 重复推导 | 同一解释在 3 处各自推导一遍 | 主文一次 + 引用 Appendix |
| Discussion 重复 Results | Discussion 大量复制 Results 数字 | 改为引用表格编号 |
| 单 seed overclaim | 单 seed 数据声称 scale-invariant | 加 preliminary/hedging 限定 |
| Registry 不同步 | Registry 面值与实际状态不一致 | 以 SSH 实测为准 |
| vLLM 静默失败 | max_model_len 太小导致 100% 400 错误 | 预检必须发真实 prompt 验证 |

---

## 八、写论文前加载的 Skills

写论文或做最终审查时，Director/Agent 应按需加载以下 skills：
- `latex-paper` — LaTeX 编译与格式
- `reference-audit` — 引用真实性审计
- `academic-writer` — ML 学术写作规范
- `paper-quality-lessons`（本 skill）— 实战经验教训

---

## 九、附录：投稿经验时间线教训

1. **论文数字锁定时机**：最终编译前 24h 锁定所有数字，之后只允许格式修改
2. **GPU 不要空闲**：审稿期间如果 Agent 空闲，应该跑 ablation/扩展实验作为 rebuttal 储备
3. **匿名化提前做**：不要等到最后一天才检查路径泄露，fresh repo 需要时间清理
4. **9 页零余量策略**：NeurIPS 正文 9 页是硬限，每次新增内容必须等量压缩并编译验证
5. **Contingency 叙事提前写**：关键实验完成前就写好两版叙事，避免最后一刻仓促改稿

16	# Step 5 — Iterative Refinement
17	
18	Step 4 全部章节落盘后，Paper Agent 进入 Step 5：把全文递交 Reviewer 评分，按反馈修改，直到收敛。
19	
20	**核心约束**：
21	- 串行——一轮 Reviewer 返回结果处理完才进下一轮，禁止并发请求
22	- 评分驱动——overall 提升才 accept 本轮，下降则 git revert
23	- 上限 5 轮——硬约束，达到上限即停，不论分数
24	
25	## 状态记录（git 是 truth source）
26	
27	每轮修改前 commit 当前论文目录，作为 revert 锚点。无需额外 state 文件。
28	
29	```
30	git -C projects/{project} add paper/
31	git -C projects/{project} commit -m "[paper] refinement round {N-1}"
32	```
33	
34	Round N 的 commit message 用 `N-1`，即 round 1 修改前 commit `round 0`（Step 4 落盘后的初稿）。
35	
36	## 单轮流程
37	
38	```
39	Round N（N = 1..5）：
40	
41	1. git commit 当前版本（message: "[paper] refinement round N-1"）
42	   └── 落地评分下降时的 revert 锚点
43	
44	2. 组装审查请求：
45	   - read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml") — 用户自定义必查项
46	   - 拼 LaTeX 全文（或 Patch 模式下的差异）+ writing_plan.yaml 路径
47	   - 末尾追加 "## 用户自定义必查项"（见下方"checklist 注入格式"）
48	
49	3. paper_agent_request_review(text=组装后的请求, project=...)
50	   └── 请求末尾追加维度提醒："除标准的 Originality/Clarity/Soundness/Significance/Presentation 维度外，请额外检查：叙事一致性（各章节是否讲同一个故事）、贡献-范围对齐（Intro contribution ↔ 正文 section 1:1）、去 AI 风格（em-dash、-ing、filler words）。参考 reviewer-audit-checklist §7。"
51	   └── Reviewer 通过 reviewer_post_to_director 回传评分
52	
53	4. 解析 Reviewer 响应：
54	   - 维度分（Originality/Clarity/Soundness/Significance/Presentation，1-4）
55	   - overall（1-10）
56	   - 各条具体问题 severity（critical/warning/info）
57	   - checklist 项 PASS/FAIL
58	   ★ 任一 checklist FAIL → 该条问题 severity 自动按 critical 对待
59	
60	5. 按问题类型分流处理：
61	   - 事实性错误（数字不一致 / 引用错位）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section 改
62	   - 段落级叙事问题（逻辑断裂 / 强度词超限）→ spawn Worker 重写段落，回来再 edit_paper_section
63	   - 结构问题（章节顺序 / 段落归并）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section
64	   - critical 且 claim 本身无支撑 → 汇报 Director（不要自行降 claim）
65	
66	6. 全部问题处理完后判断本轮 overall 走势：
67	   - overall(N) ≥ overall(N-1) → 保留本轮修改，进入收敛判断
68	   - overall(N) <  overall(N-1) → git checkout 上一轮 commit，回退本轮所有修改，标记"本轮无进展"
69	
70	7. 收敛判断（任一满足即停）：
71	   - 全部问题为 info（无 critical / warning）
72	   - N == 5（硬上限）
73	   - 连续两轮 overall 持平（差 ≤0.1）
74	   - 连续两轮无新增 critical（critical 列表内容相同或更短）
75	
76	   未收敛且 N<5 → 进入 Round N+1
77	   已收敛 → 进入收尾（见下文）
78	```

80	## checklist 注入格式
81	
82	`read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml")` 拿到 items 后，在审查请求末尾追加：

85	## 用户自定义必查项
86	以下是用户指定的必须检查的项，每项必须明确标注 PASS 或 FAIL：
87	- [chk_001] {text}
88	- [chk_002] {text}
89	...
90	
91	如果任何一项标注为 FAIL，整体 severity 自动提升为 critical（必须打回修改）。
92	```
93	
94	- checklist 为空 / 文件不存在 → 不追加该段，正常请求
95	- 不要重写 checklist 文本——保持用户原话，让 Reviewer 自己定位
96	- Dream 模式禁止注入（Dream 论文不投，格式检查无意义）

98	## 修改 Worker 任务模板
99	
100	段落级修改派 Worker（不是整章重写）时：
101	
102	```
103	spawn_worker(
104	  task_type="paper_writing",
105	  project=...,
106	  task_prompt="""

108	
109	【问题位置】{paragraph_id / 行号}

111	【建议方向】{Reviewer 给的方向}

121	- 同章节已有内容：{section}.tex 整章
122	- 引用：references.bib（只用已 verified 条目，未验证标 [UNVERIFIED]）
123	
124	要求：
125	- 只改问题段落，不动其他内容
126	- 输出修改后的段落 latex（标记 old / new）
127	- 不要画图、不要补实验
128	- 改完即返回，不写额外说明
129	"""

134	
135	## 收敛后收尾（Step 5e）
136	
137	Reviewer 评分循环收敛后**必须执行完整三件套**——视觉 + 引用 + 溯源**全部跑完**再汇报 Director；不允许只跑一两项就提交。任一发现 critical/blocker 都要在汇报中显式列出，不得"建议提交审稿"压过失败信号。
138	
139	### 三件套执行顺序
140	
141	按下面顺序串行（每一步完成才进下一步，前一步失败不绕过）：
142	
143	```
144	1. paper-visual-review 排版检查

171	### 汇报 Director 模板
172	
173	三件套全部跑完后**统一**汇报（不要分三次发），把所有 critical/warning 列在一处便于 Director 决策：
174	
175	```
176	paper_agent_post_to_director(
177	  text="[写作进展] Step 5 收尾完成
178	         迭代轮数：{N}/5
179	         最终 overall：{score}

183	         检查页数：{n}/{total}
184	         结论：PASS / 发现 X 条 critical + Y 条 warning
185	         {若有 critical：逐条列出 page + 描述}

190	         warning：mismatch X 条

195	         {若 T3 > 30% 或 TX ≥ 1：列出受影响的 claim/figure/table}

202	         C. provenance 红线触发 → 请 Director 决定：补实验 / 改 claim / 接受现状",

206	
207	Director 决定是否调 `submit_paper_to_review`——Paper Agent **不**主动调，这是 Director 的权限。
208	
209	### 红线（Step 5e 不可绕过）
210	
211	1. **三件套必须全跑**：跳过任一项直接汇报 = 违规，被 Director 打回时不接受"我以为不必要"
212	2. **critical 不静默**：视觉 critical / verify_references critical / Tier X ≥ 1 / Tier 3 > 30% 必须显式写进汇报
213	3. **不主动提交审稿**：哪怕全 PASS 也只能"建议提交"，submit_paper_to_review 是 Director 权限
214	4. **修复后必须复验**：自己修了 missing_bib → 重跑 verify_references；补 provenance → 重跑 check_provenance_completeness
215	5. **Patch 模式走 Phase E**：Patch 的收尾在 Phase E（max 3 轮 Reviewer），不复用 Step 5e 全套；Phase E 自己做 check_provenance_completeness + verify_references，视觉检查可选
216	
217	## 硬约束（与 Paper Agent 红线一致）
218	
219	1. **修改前必 git commit**——没有 commit 不开新一轮，避免 revert 失败
220	2. **未验证引用不进 .bib**——Reviewer 指出新引用需求时，先 verify_references 再写入
221	3. **checklist FAIL 项必须修复**——不参与"连续两轮无新增 critical"的轮数计数，但下一轮必须解决

description: Step 5 论文迭代修改循环——Reviewer 评分循环 + 收敛判断 + paper_checklist 注入，max 5 轮。Paper Agent 进入 Step 5 时 Read 本 skill。
scope: global
tags:

roles:

# Step 5 — Iterative Refinement

Step 4 全部章节落盘后，Paper Agent 进入 Step 5：把全文递交 Reviewer 评分，按反馈修改，直到收敛。

**核心约束**：
- 串行——一轮 Reviewer 返回结果处理完才进下一轮，禁止并发请求
- 评分驱动——overall 提升才 accept 本轮，下降则 git revert
- 上限 5 轮——硬约束，达到上限即停，不论分数

## 状态记录（git 是 truth source）

每轮修改前 commit 当前论文目录，作为 revert 锚点。无需额外 state 文件。

```
git -C projects/{project} add paper/
git -C projects/{project} commit -m "[paper] refinement round {N-1}"
```

Round N 的 commit message 用 `N-1`，即 round 1 修改前 commit `round 0`（Step 4 落盘后的初稿）。

## 单轮流程

```
Round N（N = 1..5）：

1. git commit 当前版本（message: "[paper] refinement round N-1"）
   └── 落地评分下降时的 revert 锚点

2. 组装审查请求：
   - read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml") — 用户自定义必查项
   - 拼 LaTeX 全文（或 Patch 模式下的差异）+ writing_plan.yaml 路径
   - 末尾追加 "## 用户自定义必查项"（见下方"checklist 注入格式"）

3. paper_agent_request_review(text=组装后的请求, project=...)
   └── 请求末尾追加维度提醒："除标准的 Originality/Clarity/Soundness/Significance/Presentation 维度外，请额外检查：叙事一致性（各章节是否讲同一个故事）、贡献-范围对齐（Intro contribution ↔ 正文 section 1:1）、去 AI 风格（em-dash、-ing、filler words）。参考 reviewer-audit-checklist §7。"
   └── Reviewer 通过 reviewer_post_to_director 回传评分

4. 解析 Reviewer 响应：
   - 维度分（Originality/Clarity/Soundness/Significance/Presentation，1-4）
   - overall（1-10）
   - 各条具体问题 severity（critical/warning/info）
   - checklist 项 PASS/FAIL
   ★ 任一 checklist FAIL → 该条问题 severity 自动按 critical 对待

5. 按问题类型分流处理：
   - 事实性错误（数字不一致 / 引用错位）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section 改
   - 段落级叙事问题（逻辑断裂 / 强度词超限）→ spawn Worker 重写段落，回来再 edit_paper_section
   - 结构问题（章节顺序 / 段落归并）→ 自己用 edit_paper_section
   - critical 且 claim 本身无支撑 → 汇报 Director（不要自行降 claim）

6. 全部问题处理完后判断本轮 overall 走势：
   - overall(N) ≥ overall(N-1) → 保留本轮修改，进入收敛判断
   - overall(N) <  overall(N-1) → git checkout 上一轮 commit，回退本轮所有修改，标记"本轮无进展"

7. 收敛判断（任一满足即停）：
   - 全部问题为 info（无 critical / warning）
   - N == 5（硬上限）
   - 连续两轮 overall 持平（差 ≤0.1）
   - 连续两轮无新增 critical（critical 列表内容相同或更短）

   未收敛且 N<5 → 进入 Round N+1
   已收敛 → 进入收尾（见下文）
```

## checklist 注入格式

`read_project_file("paper_checklist.yaml")` 拿到 items 后，在审查请求末尾追加：

```
## 用户自定义必查项
以下是用户指定的必须检查的项，每项必须明确标注 PASS 或 FAIL：
- [chk_001] {text}
- [chk_002] {text}
...

如果任何一项标注为 FAIL，整体 severity 自动提升为 critical（必须打回修改）。
```

- checklist 为空 / 文件不存在 → 不追加该段，正常请求
- 不要重写 checklist 文本——保持用户原话，让 Reviewer 自己定位
- Dream 模式禁止注入（Dream 论文不投，格式检查无意义）

## 修改 Worker 任务模板

段落级修改派 Worker（不是整章重写）时：

```
spawn_worker(
  task_type="paper_writing",
  project=...,
  task_prompt="""
Reviewer 在 {section} 章发现以下问题，需要你修改对应段落：

【问题位置】{paragraph_id / 行号}
【问题描述】{Reviewer 原文}
【建议方向】{Reviewer 给的方向}

当前段落原文：
```latex
{原文片段}
```

参考资料：
- 写作规范：Read skills/global/latex-paper.skill.md + red-section.skill.md
- registry 切片：{相关 exp_id 列表}
- 同章节已有内容：{section}.tex 整章
- 引用：references.bib（只用已 verified 条目，未验证标 [UNVERIFIED]）

要求：
- 只改问题段落，不动其他内容
- 输出修改后的段落 latex（标记 old / new）
- 不要画图、不要补实验
- 改完即返回，不写额外说明
"""
)
```

Worker 返回后 Paper Agent 用 `edit_paper_section(project, section, old_text=..., new_text=..., claims=..., table_cells=..., figures=...)` 落盘——`edit_paper_section` 自动同步 provenance，不会 deprecate 未触及的 claim。

## 收敛后收尾（Step 5e）

Reviewer 评分循环收敛后**必须执行完整三件套**——视觉 + 引用 + 溯源**全部跑完**再汇报 Director；不允许只跑一两项就提交。任一发现 critical/blocker 都要在汇报中显式列出，不得"建议提交审稿"压过失败信号。

### 三件套执行顺序

按下面顺序串行（每一步完成才进下一步，前一步失败不绕过）：

```
1. paper-visual-review 排版检查
   └── Read skills/global/paper-visual-review.skill.md
   └── pdf_to_images(pdf_path=projects/{project}/paper/main.pdf, pages="1-N", dpi=200)
       逐页检查图表分辨率 / 字号 / 边距溢出 / 公式 / 引用编号 / 缺失引用占位 [?]
   └── cleanup_pdf_images(output_dir=<上一步返回的 output_dir>)  # 不留临时文件
   └── 收集 findings：[{page, severity, issue}]
   └── 出现 critical（图表溢出 / 缺失编号 / 公式乱码）→ 记入 visual_report，**不**立即返工，
       与 verify_references / check_provenance_completeness 的结果**一并汇报 Director**

2. verify_references 最终引用验证
   └── verify_references(paper_dir="projects/{project}/paper", project=..., skip_online=False)
   └── 返回字段：status (ok/orphan_bib/missing_bib/not_found/mismatch) 按条聚合
   └── critical 阈值：
        - missing_bib（正文 \cite 但 .bib 缺）→ 必须修，否则 LaTeX 编译失败
        - not_found（OpenAlex 找不到）→ 疑似幻觉引用，自己 WebSearch 二次验证；仍找不到 → critical
        - mismatch（年份/作者偏差）→ warning
   └── 自己能改的小问题（missing_bib、年份） → edit_paper_section 修；改完**再调一次 verify_references** 确认通过

3. check_provenance_completeness 溯源覆盖
   └── check_provenance_completeness(project=...)
   └── 返回：tier_distribution / untracked_numbers / invalidated_claims
   └── 关键阈值：
        - Tier 3 占比 > 30% → 必须汇报 Director（红线，不得静默交付）
        - Tier X（invalidated，实验失败/被作废）≥ 1 条 → critical：claim 失去支撑，汇报 Director 决策是否改 claim
        - untracked_numbers（正文出现但 provenance 没追踪的数字）≥ 5 → warning：派 Worker 补 provenance
```

### 汇报 Director 模板

三件套全部跑完后**统一**汇报（不要分三次发），把所有 critical/warning 列在一处便于 Director 决策：

```
paper_agent_post_to_director(
  text="[写作进展] Step 5 收尾完成
         迭代轮数：{N}/5
         最终 overall：{score}
         checklist：全部 PASS / 还有 X 条 FAIL（已修复 / 待 Director 决策）

         ===== 视觉检查 =====
         检查页数：{n}/{total}
         结论：PASS / 发现 X 条 critical + Y 条 warning
         {若有 critical：逐条列出 page + 描述}

         ===== 引用验证 =====
         总数 X 条，已验证 Y 条
         critical：missing_bib X 条 + 疑似幻觉 Y 条（已尝试 WebSearch 二次验证 → 结果）
         warning：mismatch X 条
         {若有 critical：列出条目 + 已采取的修复}

         ===== Provenance 覆盖 =====
         Tier 分布：T1 {a}% / T2 {b}% / T3 {c}% / TX {d}%
         {若 T3 > 30% 或 TX ≥ 1：列出受影响的 claim/figure/table}
         未追踪数字：X 个（详见 untracked_numbers）

         ===== 建议 =====
         {以下任选其一}
         A. 视觉/引用/provenance 全部 PASS → 建议提交审稿（submit_paper_to_review）
         B. 存在 critical → 请 Director 决策：{具体问题列表 + 建议修复方向}
         C. provenance 红线触发 → 请 Director 决定：补实验 / 改 claim / 接受现状",
  project=...
)
```

Director 决定是否调 `submit_paper_to_review`——Paper Agent **不**主动调，这是 Director 的权限。

### 红线（Step 5e 不可绕过）

1. **三件套必须全跑**：跳过任一项直接汇报 = 违规，被 Director 打回时不接受"我以为不必要"
2. **critical 不静默**：视觉 critical / verify_references critical / Tier X ≥ 1 / Tier 3 > 30% 必须显式写进汇报
3. **不主动提交审稿**：哪怕全 PASS 也只能"建议提交"，submit_paper_to_review 是 Director 权限
4. **修复后必须复验**：自己修了 missing_bib → 重跑 verify_references；补 provenance → 重跑 check_provenance_completeness
5. **Patch 模式走 Phase E**：Patch 的收尾在 Phase E（max 3 轮 Reviewer），不复用 Step 5e 全套；Phase E 自己做 check_provenance_completeness + verify_references，视觉检查可选

## 硬约束（与 Paper Agent 红线一致）

1. **修改前必 git commit**——没有 commit 不开新一轮，避免 revert 失败
2. **未验证引用不进 .bib**——Reviewer 指出新引用需求时，先 verify_references 再写入
3. **checklist FAIL 项必须修复**——不参与"连续两轮无新增 critical"的轮数计数，但下一轮必须解决
4. **overall 下降必 revert**——不允许"将就一下"
5. **不自行降 claim**——claim 无支撑是 Director 决策，Paper Agent 只能改表述强度，不能改 claim 内容
6. **Patch / Dream 模式不走本 skill**——Patch 走 Phase E（max 3 轮），Dream 跳过 Reviewer 迭代

## 与 Reviewer 评分模板的合约

Reviewer 在 `prompts/roles/reviewer.md` §5.3 已规定返回格式：

```
[写作评审] 轮次 N/5
维度评分（1-4）：Originality / Clarity / Soundness / Significance / Presentation
Overall（1-10）：
## 用户自定义必查项（如审查请求含 paper_checklist）
- [chk_id]: PASS / FAIL — 理由
## 具体问题
- [severity] 位置 + 描述 + 建议
```

Paper Agent 解析时按位置抓字段——Reviewer 偶尔会漏维度分，**漏了的当作 4（满分）处理**，避免误判 overall 下降。

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

Representation engineering \citep{zou2023repe} reveals that large language models encode sycophancy as a linear direction in their residual streams.
A contrastive sycophancy direction $\dsyc$, extracted from style-controlled pairs of valid belief revision and sycophantic capitulation, achieves cross-validated AUROC $0.827 \pm 0.028$ on Qwen3-8B and $0.779 \pm 0.019$ on Llama-3-8B (\S\ref{sec:direction_quality}).
The direction captures evidential granularity: discriminability rises monotonically from weak-evidence pairs (AUROC 0.675) through medium (0.883) to strong (0.929), and the signal remains stable under LoRA training with cosine drift of approximately 0.96 at 500 steps.
These results, replicated across two architecturally distinct model families, point to an appealing possibility: if the model's representations already separate sycophantic from non-sycophantic behavior, that separation should be convertible into a reward signal for reinforcement learning.
Sycophancy is among the most persistent alignment failures in deployed systems \citep{sharma2023sycophancy}, and a representation-level reward could complement existing behavioral approaches by targeting the internal computation rather than its surface outputs.

This paper shows that the conversion fails, and that the failure runs deeper than the representation signal itself.
We test three formulations that translate $\dsyc$ into a GRPO \citep{shao2024grpo} training signal (cosine similarity, scaled cosine, and binary probe) across six experimental configurations; every formulation fails.
Cosine similarity produces a reward gap of just 0.098 between valid and sycophantic activations, too narrow to drive policy updates (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}).
Online recalibration improves the offline AUROC from 0.82 to 0.91 yet triggers mode collapse.
A binary probe with stopped gradients creates a stubbornness trap: the model learns that never revising its answer reliably collects the probe reward, and the true-positive flip rate ($\tof$) drops to zero within 500 steps while generation entropy remains at 0.70 (\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}).
These failures might suggest that removing $\dsyc$ in favor of a purely behavioral reward would resolve the problem.
It does not.
R3-only GRPO, which uses an NLI-based behavioral reward without any representation component, also fails to calibrate sycophancy: the \sycon{} score starts at 0.074 at checkpoint 1000, reaches only 0.114 by checkpoint 5000, and never exceeds the vanilla baseline of 0.134 (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
The trajectory shows partial recovery before plateauing: the score stalls at 0.114 between checkpoints 4000 and 5000, 15\% below vanilla with no further improvement.
Two layers of failure emerge: $\dsyc$-based rewards are actively harmful, and GRPO itself is structurally insufficient for sycophancy calibration.

Existing approaches to sycophancy mitigation span three categories.
Representation-based inference methods, including activation addition \citep{turner2023actadd} and contrastive activation addition \citep{rimsky2024caa}, steer model behavior at test time without modifying weights.
RL-based training methods use scalar rewards to update policy through reinforcement learning; our $\dsyc$ GRPO variants and R3-only GRPO both fall into this category, as does representation-guided RL more broadly \citep{zhang2026latentgrpo}.
SFT-based training takes a fundamentally different approach: ACT \citep{consistency2025bctact} applies supervised fine-tuning with an L2 activation consistency loss that provides dense per-token supervision rather than a single scalar per completion.
ACT achieves a \sycon{} score of 0.301 at checkpoint 8000, more than double the vanilla baseline, while every GRPO variant remains below it (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
The contrast is informative.
Techniques for discovering latent knowledge \citep{burns2023ccs} and representation-guided RL share a premise: a direction with high discriminability in activation space should transfer into a useful training signal.
For reasoning faithfulness and safety refusal, this premise holds, because the behavior to suppress is geometrically distinct from the behavior to preserve along the relevant direction.
Sycophancy violates this premise.
Capitulation under social pressure and revision under valid evidence produce overlapping activation signatures along $\dsyc$, because both involve the model shifting its stated belief toward the user's position.

The root cause is a semantic gap between discriminability and reward utility.
$\dsyc$ encodes \emph{whether} belief changed, not \emph{whether it should have}.
A post-hoc classifier can use this signal effectively because it scores labeled examples where the validity of the belief change is already known.
A reward signal during RL training has no such access to ground truth; it must distinguish warranted revision from unwarranted capitulation using activation geometry alone, and $\dsyc$ collapses exactly this distinction.
This conflation explains both layers of failure.
$\dsyc$ rewards penalize all belief change indiscriminately, producing behavioral collapse.
R3-only GRPO's single scalar per completion cannot compensate because it lacks the per-token resolution to teach which belief changes are warranted and which are not.
ACT succeeds because its dense supervision operates at the token level, where the valid/invalid distinction can be resolved.
Sycophancy is defined relative to external evidential warrant \citep{sharma2023sycophancy}, a property that no single activation direction can fully encode.
The entanglement between helpfulness and sycophancy at the representation level, where the same mechanisms that allow models to track user intent also predispose them to capitulate \citep{wang2025internal}, is amplified by RLHF \citep{shapira2026amplifies}.
When reward overoptimization \citep{gao2023scaling} operates on a signal that conflates compliance with capitulation, the result is predictable collapse \citep{casper2023openproblems}.

We present three contributions:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{All GRPO approaches fail for sycophancy calibration} (C1). We extract and validate $\dsyc$ on two model families (Qwen3-8B AUROC $0.827 \pm 0.028$; Llama-3-8B AUROC $0.779 \pm 0.019$), then show that all three $\dsyc$-based reward formulations produce behavioral collapse (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}, \S\ref{sec:probe_trap}). R3-only GRPO, which removes $\dsyc$ entirely, also fails: \sycon{} reaches only 0.114 at checkpoint 5000 against a vanilla baseline of 0.134 (\S\ref{sec:discussion}). Discriminability does not confer reward utility, and sparse RL rewards are structurally insufficient for this task.

\item \textbf{Probe reward trap with behavioral-before-distributional collapse} (C2). The binary probe reward produces behavioral death ($\tof = 0$ at step 500) while entropy remains at 0.70. The 1,300-step lag before distributional collapse means standard entropy monitoring misses the failure entirely, with the reward averaging $+0.72$ throughout (\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}).

\item \textbf{Sparse RL reward cannot convey the valid/invalid distinction} (C3). We trace all failures to a unified root cause: $\dsyc$ encodes belief-change direction but not evidential warrant. A single scalar reward per completion, whether from representations or behavioral classifiers, cannot teach the model which belief changes are warranted. Dense SFT supervision resolves this: ACT achieves \sycon{} of 0.301, while all GRPO variants remain below vanilla (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
\end{itemize}
\section{Experimental Framework}
\label{sec:framework}

\subsection{Direction Extraction}
\label{ssec:extraction}

We extract a linear sycophancy direction $\dsyc$ from the residual stream using contrastive activation pairs: a \emph{valid correction} (warranted belief revision under strong evidence) and a \emph{sycophantic capitulation} (unwarranted concession under social pressure), style-controlled to match hedging, politeness, and length.
From 181 paired examples stratified across three evidence-strength levels (362 activations total), we compute the mean difference at target layer $\ell$:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:dsyc}
\dsyc = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\left(\mathbf{h}^{+}_i - \mathbf{h}^{-}_i\right)
\end{equation}
where $\mathbf{h}^{+}_i$ and $\mathbf{h}^{-}_i$ are residual-stream activations for the $i$-th valid and sycophantic response.
The target layer is selected by 5-fold cross-validated AUROC; on Qwen3-8B this yields layer 19 with AUROC $0.827 \pm 0.028$.

\subsection{Reward Formulations}
\label{ssec:reward}

GRPO \citep{shao2024grpo} ranks sampled completions by reward and updates the policy toward higher-reward outputs.
We define $R = w_1 \cdot \rone + w_3 \cdot \rthree$, where $\rone$ is a direction-based component and $\rthree$ is a behavioral component (DeBERTa NLI classifier scoring consistency with the ground-truth answer).
Three formulations translate $\dsyc$ into $\rone$:
\begin{itemize}
\item[\textbf{F1}] \textbf{Cosine.} $\rone = \cos(\mathbf{h},\, \dsyc)$.
\item[\textbf{F2}] \textbf{Scaled cosine.} $\rone = \alpha \cdot \cos(\mathbf{h},\, \dsyc)$, amplifying gradient magnitude.
\item[\textbf{F3}] \textbf{Binary probe.} $\rone = \mathbb{I}[P(\text{syc} \mid \mathbf{h}) < 0.5]$, a frozen logistic probe with stopped gradients.
\end{itemize}
As an ablation, R3-only GRPO sets $w_1{=}0$, training with only the behavioral reward.

\subsection{Online Recalibration}
\label{ssec:recalib}

LoRA fine-tuning shifts internal representations, so we re-extract $\dsyc$ every 500 steps.
The cosine similarity between consecutive directions remains ${\approx}\,0.96$ at step 500, indicating slow drift relative to recalibration frequency.

\subsection{SFT Baseline: Activation Consistency Training}
\label{ssec:baselines}

ACT \citep{consistency2025bctact} combines standard SFT loss with an L2 activation consistency loss at target layers, providing dense per-token supervision.
Unlike GRPO's single scalar per completion, ACT operates at the token level using labeled valid/invalid pairs.

\subsection{Evaluation}
\label{ssec:eval}

The \emph{True-positive Flip rate} ($\tof$) measures acceptance of valid corrections; the \emph{No-Flip rate} ($\nof$) measures resistance to invalid pressure.
Their harmonic mean captures the calibration trade-off:
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:sycon}
\sycon = \frac{2 \cdot \tof \cdot \nof}{\tof + \nof}
\end{equation}
Flip classification uses NLI following \citet{consistency2025bctact}.
All experiments use Qwen3-8B with LoRA (rank$=$64, $\alpha{=}128$) and DeepSpeed ZeRO-2.
\section{Direction Discriminability}
\label{sec:direction_quality}

Before evaluating $\dsyc$ as a reward signal (\S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}--\S\ref{sec:probe_trap}), we first establish that it captures a genuine sycophancy-related signal in the residual stream.
If the direction failed to discriminate sycophantic from non-sycophantic activations, downstream reward failures would be trivially explained by poor direction quality rather than by a fundamental gap between discriminability and reward utility.
We evaluate discriminability along five axes: cross-validated classification accuracy, evidence-strength stratification, cross-model transfer, training stability, and probe ablation.
Figure~\ref{fig:direction_quality} summarizes the per-layer AUROC profiles for both models.

\paragraph{Qwen3-8B layer-wise discriminability.}
We evaluate $\dsyc$ via 5-fold cross-validated AUROC on 181 style-controlled contrastive pairs (\S\ref{ssec:extraction}).
The direction achieves AUROC $0.827 \pm 0.028$ at its best layer (L19).
Discriminability emerges gradually across depth: layers L0--L8 perform near chance, statistical significance ($p < 0.01$) first appears at L16, and performance peaks at L19.
This gradual emergence, with the peak in the upper third of the network, suggests that sycophancy-relevant information is encoded as a late-stage representation rather than an input-level confound.
The direction also captures evidential granularity.
AUROC rises monotonically from 0.675 on weak-evidence pairs to 0.883 on medium and 0.929 on strong pairs.
This gradient indicates that $\dsyc$ encodes the degree of evidential warrant, not merely a binary sycophancy label.

\paragraph{Cross-model generalization.}
To rule out that these results are specific to Qwen3-8B's representation geometry, we repeat the full extraction and evaluation pipeline on Llama-3-8B-Instruct.
Table~\ref{tab:cross_model} compares the two models.
Llama-3-8B achieves CV AUROC $0.779 \pm 0.019$ at L16, with a parallel evidence-strength gradient (weak 0.711, medium 0.864, strong 0.911).
The best-layer depth differs (L16 vs.\ L19), consistent with the architectural differences between the two families, but the qualitative pattern is identical: gradual emergence, best-layer selection in the upper third, and monotonic strength scaling.
Discriminability is robust across knowledge domains, with per-domain AUROCs on Llama-3-8B ranging from 0.751 (geography) to 0.844 (commonsense).
When surface confounds (response length, hedging patterns) are explicitly controlled, Llama-3-8B's AUROC rises to 0.923, which confirms that the direction captures semantic content rather than stylistic artifacts.
The consistent results across architecturally distinct model families indicate that contrastive sycophancy directions reflect a shared representational phenomenon rather than a model-specific idiosyncrasy.

\paragraph{Training stability and probe ablation.}
Two additional analyses confirm the robustness of $\dsyc$ under training dynamics.
First, we track direction drift during LoRA fine-tuning: at step 500, the cosine similarity between the original and re-extracted $\dsyc$ is approximately 0.96, and per-layer AUROC remains above 0.77.
The direction drifts slowly relative to the 500-step recalibration interval (\S\ref{ssec:recalib}), so the reward signal does not become stale between updates.
Second, we compare $\dsyc$ against a random baseline: a logistic probe trained on the learned direction achieves AUROC 0.835, versus 0.727 for a probe trained on a random direction of equal dimensionality ($\Delta{=}{+}0.108$).
The learned direction carries substantially more sycophancy-relevant information than an arbitrary axis in the same activation space.

\paragraph{Implications for reward design.}
These results establish that $\dsyc$ reliably separates sycophantic from non-sycophantic representations across models, evidence-strength levels, and training checkpoints.
Direction quality is not the bottleneck.
The reward failures documented in \S\ref{sec:cosine_failure}--\S\ref{sec:probe_trap} therefore cannot be attributed to a noisy or degenerate direction; they point to a deeper incompatibility between discriminability and reward utility.
\section{Cosine \texorpdfstring{$\rone$}{R1}: Structural Failure}
\label{sec:cosine_failure}

Section~\ref{sec:direction_quality} established that $\dsyc$ achieves AUROC 0.827 on Qwen3-8B.
We now test whether this discriminability translates into a viable GRPO reward.
Four configurations form a diagnostic chain (Table~\ref{tab:cosine_chain}): each resolves the failure mode of its predecessor but exposes a deeper limitation.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Cosine $\rone$ failure chain on Qwen3-8B (LoRA rank$=$64, GRPO with $R = w_1 \cdot \rone + w_3 \cdot \rthree$).}
\label{tab:cosine_chain}
\begin{tabular}{lllll}
\toprule
Config & $\rone$ Formula & $w_1$ & Outcome & Root Cause \\
\midrule
F1a & $\tanh(\mathbf{h}\cdot\dsyc/20)$ & 0.25 & Gate saturation & Norm mismatch \\
F1b & $\cos(\mathbf{h},\, \dsyc)$ & 0.25 & $\rone \approx 0$ & Gap too small \\
F1c & +recalibration & 0.25 & Mode collapse & Reward discontinuity \\
F1d & $5\cos(\mathbf{h},\, \dsyc)$ & 0.40 & Mode collapse & $\rthree$ saturation \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

F1a uses a dot-product formulation ($\rone = \tanh(\mathbf{h} \cdot \dsyc / 20)$), but residual-stream norms exceed the direction norm by $100$--$1{,}200{\times}$, saturating the tanh gate and zeroing the gradient by step 955.
Switching to cosine similarity (F1b) eliminates norm dependence, yet the cosine gap between valid and sycophantic activations averages only 0.098 across layers---too narrow to generate meaningful reward contrast.
Online recalibration (F1c, \S\ref{ssec:recalib}) raises offline AUROC from 0.82 to 0.91 but paradoxically triggers mode collapse: the abrupt shift in $\dsyc$ at each recalibration event creates a reward discontinuity that destabilizes GRPO advantage estimates, collapsing entropy to 0.069 within 300 steps.
Amplifying the signal with $5{\times}$ scaling (F1d) lifts $\rone$ above the noise floor but simultaneously amplifies the conflation between warranted revision and unwarranted capitulation; $\rthree$ saturates at 0.9998 by step 300, leaving the noisy $\rone$ as the sole gradient source until terminal collapse at step 2160.

The four configurations converge on a single conclusion: $\dsyc$ encodes the \emph{direction} of belief change but not whether that change is \emph{warranted}.
Valid revision and sycophantic capitulation both shift activations toward the user's position along $\dsyc$, so the cosine projection assigns similar scores to both.
This is not a calibration artifact---recalibration improves discriminability yet rewards still fail---but a semantic limitation of any continuous $\dsyc$-based reward.
Section~\ref{sec:probe_trap} examines whether discretizing the signal via a binary probe can escape this limitation.
\section{The Probe Reward Trap}
\label{sec:probe_trap}

The cosine formulations fail because the continuous projection of $\dsyc$ produces a gap too narrow for reward contrast.
A natural remedy is to discretize: train a logistic probe on $\dsyc$ and threshold its output, yielding $\rone = \mathbb{I}[P(\text{syc} \mid \mathbf{h}) < 0.5]$ (F3 in \S\ref{ssec:reward}).
We show that this discretization sidesteps the magnitude problem but creates a qualitatively worse failure.

\paragraph{Differentiable probe: gradient gaming.}
Without stop-gradient (exp-008), the policy discovers within ${\sim}30$ steps that shifting activations away from the sycophancy cluster maximizes $\rone$ regardless of response content, producing an inverted profile ($\tof = 0.978$, $\nof = 0.006$).
This motivates the frozen-probe design below.

\paragraph{Binary probe: the stubbornness trap.}
With stop-gradient (exp-008v3), the policy cannot game the boundary but instead exploits a deeper flaw: $\dsyc$ does not condition on input validity, so refusing to revise a wrong answer receives the same $\rone = 1$ as correctly resisting invalid pressure.
By step 500, $\tof$ drops to 0.000 and $\nof$ reaches 0.995, yielding $\sycon = 0$.

\paragraph{Behavioral death precedes distributional collapse.}

Table~\ref{tab:probe_trajectory} reveals a 1{,}300-step lag between behavioral and distributional collapse.
At step 500, the model is behaviorally dead ($\tof = 0$) yet entropy remains at 0.70---well within the range that standard monitors would flag as healthy---and the combined reward averages $+0.72$ because both $\rone$ and $\rthree$ reinforce non-flipping.
Entropy does not collapse until step ${\sim}1840$.
This gap carries a practical warning: entropy-based early stopping, the most common safeguard against reward hacking~\citep{casper2023openproblems}, would miss the failure entirely.
Detecting probe reward traps requires behavioral monitoring (periodic $\tof$ evaluation), not distributional monitoring alone.

\paragraph{A dilemma for direction-based rewards.}
The differentiable and binary failures bracket the design space.
With gradients, the policy games the boundary; without gradients, it exploits the fact that stubbornness and genuine resistance are indistinguishable along $\dsyc$.
Any reward conditioned only on $\dsyc$---continuous or discrete, differentiable or frozen---will either be gamed or will reward rigidity.
Escaping this dilemma requires a signal that incorporates the evidential warrant of the user's challenge, a dimension that $\dsyc$ does not encode~\citep{denison2024subterfuge}.
\section{Analysis: Discriminability $\neq$ Reward Utility}\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Unified root cause.}
The failures in Sections~\ref{sec:cosine_failure} and~\ref{sec:probe_trap} trace to a single geometric limitation.
$\dsyc$ encodes the \emph{direction} of belief change but not its \emph{evidential warrant}: valid revision and sycophantic capitulation both shift activations toward the user's position along the same direction.
The two reward families expose complementary faces of this blindness.
Cosine $\rone$ penalizes all belief change indiscriminately; the resulting mode collapse (F1c, F1d) reflects excessive punishment of any activation shift along $\dsyc$.
The binary probe $\rone$ rewards all resistance regardless of input validity; the stubbornness trap ($\tof = 0$ by step 500) reflects excessive permissiveness toward activation stasis.
These are not independent design flaws but dual consequences of a direction that conflates the target behavior (resisting invalid challenges) with its complement (refusing valid corrections).
Cross-model evidence confirms the limitation extends beyond Qwen3-8B: Llama-3-8B independently achieves AUROC $0.779 \pm 0.019$ on the same contrastive pairs with the same monotonic evidence gradient, so discriminability generalizes across architectures while the semantic gap between discriminability and reward utility persists.
This pattern contrasts with reasoning faithfulness and safety directions~\citep{zhang2026latentgrpo}, where the behavior to suppress is geometrically distinct from the behavior to preserve along the relevant direction.
For sycophancy, the target and its complement occupy the same activation region; they differ only in whether external evidence warrants the belief change.

It does not.
The $\sycon$ trajectory shows partial recovery that stalls: 0.074 at checkpoint 1000, 0.085 at checkpoint 2000, 0.095 at checkpoint 3000, and 0.114 at both checkpoints 4000 and 5000.
Recovery halts entirely between checkpoints 4000 and 5000, plateauing 15\% below the vanilla baseline of 0.134 with no further improvement.
ActAdd~\citep{turner2023actadd}, the inference-time baseline, achieves only $\sycon = 0.054$, confirming that activation-level intervention without weight updates cannot resolve the calibration problem.

\paragraph{Why SFT succeeds where GRPO fails.}
ACT~\citep{consistency2025bctact} achieves $\sycon = 0.301$ at checkpoint 8000, more than $2{\times}$ the vanilla baseline and above every RL and inference-time variant (Table~\ref{tab:main_comparison}).
The ACT trajectory is not monotonic: $\sycon = 0.255$ at checkpoint 2000, dips to 0.214 at checkpoint 4000 ($-4.1$ percentage points as $\tof$ drops and $\nof$ rises), recovers to 0.262 at checkpoint 6000, and reaches 0.301 at checkpoint 8000.
ACT also experiences stubbornness episodes, yet it recovers from them (Figure~\ref{fig:trajectory}).
The critical difference is supervision density.
SFT provides a corrective gradient at every token position in every training example: when the model begins to resist valid corrections, per-token cross-entropy loss immediately penalizes the incorrect tokens and supplies gradient information about \emph{which} outputs need to change.
GRPO provides one scalar per completion; once the policy locks into stubbornness, that scalar reinforces the behavior because consistent non-flipping collects high reward from both $\rone$ and $\rthree$.
Dense per-token loss can break out of stubbornness equilibria that sparse per-completion reward cannot escape.
This recovery capacity is the practical signature of the dense-versus-sparse supervision gap.
ACT is also far more efficient: its checkpoint 500 ($\sycon = 0.170$) already exceeds the plateau that $\rthree$-only GRPO reaches after 5000 steps of training.
